title: Web Development Basics
description: Learn core web foundations and responsive interface basics.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of semantic HTML?
options: Describe the meaning and structure of content
questions.explanation: Semantic elements communicate the role of page content to browsers and assistive technology.

questions.prompt: Which language is primarily responsible for styling a web page?
questions.explanation: CSS controls layout, colors, typography, and other visual presentation.

questions.prompt: What does responsive design aim to support?
options: Layouts that adapt to different screen sizes
questions.explanation: Responsive layouts adapt content and controls for different viewport sizes.

questions.prompt: Which HTML element is best suited for a page's main content?
questions.explanation: The main element identifies the dominant content of a document.

questions.prompt: What does a CSS media query commonly evaluate?
questions.explanation: Media queries apply styles conditionally, often based on viewport width.

questions.prompt: Why should form controls have associated labels?
options: To provide an accessible name and clickable label
questions.explanation: Labels help screen-reader users identify controls and improve the click target.

questions.prompt: Which CSS layout system is designed for two-dimensional rows and columns?
questions.explanation: CSS Grid provides two-dimensional row-and-column layout.

questions.prompt: What is the DOM?
options: A structured representation of a document that scripts can access
questions.explanation: The DOM represents document nodes and exposes them to browser APIs.

questions.prompt: Which attribute provides alternative text for an informative image?
questions.explanation: The alt attribute supplies a text alternative when an image conveys information.

questions.prompt: What is a sensible first step when a page overflows on mobile?
options: Inspect its layout and test at a narrow viewport
questions.explanation: Testing at the target viewport helps locate fixed widths and other overflow causes.

title: Python Foundations
description: Build foundational Python and computational thinking skills.

questions.prompt: Which Python type represents a sequence that cannot be changed after creation?
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable sequences; lists can be changed.

questions.prompt: What does a for loop do?
options: Repeats a block over an iterable
questions.explanation: A for loop iterates over items from an iterable.

questions.prompt: What is the usual purpose of a function?
questions.explanation: Functions name reusable blocks of behavior and can accept inputs.

questions.prompt: Which value represents the absence of a value in Python?
questions.explanation: Python uses None for the absence of a value.

questions.prompt: What is a dictionary commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Dictionaries store key-value mappings.

questions.prompt: What does an if statement enable?
questions.explanation: An if statement chooses behavior based on a condition.

questions.prompt: Why use a virtual environment for a Python project?
questions.explanation: Virtual environments isolate installed packages for a project.

questions.prompt: What does a pandas DataFrame represent?
questions.explanation: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labeled data structure.

questions.prompt: What is an exception?
options: An event that interrupts normal program flow
questions.explanation: Exceptions report errors or unusual conditions during execution.

questions.prompt: What is a good way to check a small function?
options: Try representative inputs and expected edge cases
Assume it works from its name
questions.explanation: Testing representative and edge inputs helps verify behavior.

title: C and Embedded Programming Basics
description: Review C programming foundations and an introductory embedded-C course.

questions.prompt: Which function is the conventional entry point of a hosted C program?
questions.explanation: A hosted C program begins execution in main.

questions.prompt: What is the index of the first element in a C array?
questions.explanation: C arrays use zero-based indexing.

questions.prompt: Which operator obtains the address of an object?
questions.explanation: The unary & operator produces an object's address.

questions.prompt: What does sizeof return?
options: The size in bytes of a type or object
The number of array values always
questions.explanation: sizeof yields the number of bytes occupied by its operand's type.

questions.prompt: Which format specifier is commonly used to print an int with printf?
questions.explanation: %d is used for a signed decimal integer in printf.

questions.prompt: What is a pointer?
options: An object that stores an address
questions.explanation: A pointer stores the address of another object or function.

questions.prompt: What does break do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: break terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a header file?
questions.explanation: Headers commonly provide declarations shared between source files.

questions.prompt: What does a function parameter represent?
options: An input supplied to a function
questions.explanation: Parameters let a function receive values from its caller.

questions.prompt: Why should a program check array bounds?
options: C does not automatically enforce array bounds
questions.explanation: Out-of-bounds access has undefined behavior in C.

title: Data and AI Foundations
description: Explore data preparation, analytics projects, and machine-learning fundamentals.

questions.prompt: What is a common first step before analyzing a dataset?
options: Train a model without checking it
questions.explanation: Inspection and thoughtful cleaning help identify quality problems before analysis.

questions.prompt: What is a feature in a supervised learning dataset?
options: An input variable used to make predictions
questions.explanation: Features are input variables used by a model.

questions.prompt: What is a target label?
options: The value a supervised model is trained to predict
questions.explanation: The target is the outcome associated with each training example.

questions.prompt: Why separate training and test data?
options: To estimate performance on unseen examples
To remove the need for evaluation
questions.explanation: A held-out test set helps assess generalization to unseen data.

questions.prompt: What is overfitting?
options: A model fits training details but performs poorly on new data
A model has too few rows
A chart has too many labels
A database uses a primary key
questions.explanation: Overfit models capture noise or training-specific patterns and generalize poorly.

questions.prompt: Which pandas structure is two-dimensional and tabular?
questions.explanation: A DataFrame organizes tabular data in labeled rows and columns.

questions.prompt: What does a SQL SELECT statement do?
options: Reads data from a table or query
questions.explanation: SELECT retrieves data from relational tables or other query sources.

questions.prompt: Why document a data project?
options: To explain data, methods, assumptions, and results
To guarantee a model is unbiased
questions.explanation: Documentation makes the project understandable and reproducible.

questions.prompt: What is a baseline model useful for?
questions.explanation: A baseline helps assess whether a more complex approach adds value.

questions.prompt: What is an important practice when sharing a data portfolio?
options: Avoid exposing personal or confidential data
questions.explanation: Portfolio data should respect privacy and be presented with accurate limitations.

title: Resume and Interview Preparation
description: Prepare a truthful student application and practice interview fundamentals.

questions.prompt: What should a student without job experience emphasize on a resume?
questions.explanation: Relevant projects and coursework can demonstrate skills without overstating experience.

questions.prompt: What makes a resume bullet more informative?
options: A clear action and truthful result or scope
questions.explanation: Specific, accurate actions and outcomes make experience easier to understand.

questions.prompt: What should a tailored cover letter do?
options: Connect relevant evidence to the role
Use the same company name everywhere
questions.explanation: A focused letter connects the applicant's relevant evidence to the position.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate in a professional recruiter message?
options: A concise introduction and a specific, respectful request
questions.explanation: Concise, respectful outreach is easier for a recruiter to respond to.

questions.prompt: How should a student describe a project they did not complete alone?
questions.explanation: Clearly describing individual contributions is honest and useful.

questions.prompt: What is a useful structure for 'Tell me about yourself'?
options: Relevant background, evidence, and role interest
questions.explanation: A concise, role-related answer gives the interviewer useful context.

questions.prompt: If you do not know an interview answer, what is a constructive response?
options: Be honest and explain how you would reason or learn
questions.explanation: Honest reasoning can demonstrate problem-solving even when a fact is unfamiliar.

questions.prompt: What should you do before sending an application?
options: Check the role details and proofread your materials
questions.explanation: Reviewing the listing and materials helps catch errors and assess legitimacy.

questions.prompt: Which LinkedIn profile practice is most appropriate?
options: Use accurate experience and a clear student headline
Claim skills you do not have
questions.explanation: Accurate profile information makes your background clear and credible.

questions.prompt: What is a useful way to prepare for an interview?
options: Practice concise examples and research the role
questions.explanation: Practice and role research support relevant, truthful answers.

title: UI/UX Foundations
description: Practice user research, wireframing, and portfolio case-study basics.

questions.prompt: What is the goal of user research?
options: Prove a design is already perfect
questions.explanation: Research helps designers understand people and the context in which they use a product.

questions.prompt: What is a wireframe?
options: A simplified representation of structure and layout
questions.explanation: Wireframes communicate basic page structure before visual polish.

questions.prompt: What is a prototype useful for?
options: Exploring and testing an interaction before implementation
Guaranteeing the product has no bugs
questions.explanation: Prototypes let teams explore ideas and gather feedback early.

questions.prompt: What should a design case study explain?
options: The problem, process, decisions, and outcome
questions.explanation: A case study should make the design problem-solving process understandable.

questions.prompt: Why test a design with representative users?
options: To discover usability issues and learn from behavior
questions.explanation: Usability testing reveals where people struggle and what may need revision.

questions.prompt: What is a useful accessibility practice for text and backgrounds?
options: Use color as the only instruction
questions.explanation: Sufficient contrast improves readability for many users.

questions.prompt: What does visual hierarchy help users understand?
options: Which content is most important and how it relates
questions.explanation: Hierarchy helps guide attention through content and actions.

questions.prompt: When should a designer iterate on a prototype?
options: When feedback or testing reveals a useful change
Whenever a random color is available
questions.explanation: Iteration uses evidence and feedback to improve a solution.

questions.prompt: What should a portfolio screenshot avoid?
options: Exposing private or sensitive user data
questions.explanation: Portfolios should protect privacy and remove sensitive information.

questions.prompt: What is a good way to frame a design decision?
options: Explain the constraint, evidence, and trade-off
questions.explanation: Explaining evidence and trade-offs makes design reasoning transparent.

title: Cybersecurity Foundations
description: Review network defense, secure web application practices, and common security concepts.

questions.prompt: What is the main goal of confidentiality in information security?
options: Guarantee that software has no bugs
questions.explanation: Confidentiality limits information access to authorized people and systems.

questions.prompt: How does authentication differ from authorization?
options: Authentication verifies identity; authorization determines permitted actions
Authentication grants every permission; authorization encrypts data
Authorization verifies identity; authentication sets network routes
questions.explanation: Authentication checks who a user is, while authorization checks what that identity may do.

questions.prompt: How should an application store user passwords?
options: With a purpose-built password hash and unique salt
questions.explanation: Password storage should use a password-hashing function with a unique salt, not reversible plaintext.

questions.prompt: What does the principle of least privilege recommend?
options: Grant only the access needed for a task
Share one account among all users
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces unnecessary access and limits the impact of mistakes or compromise.

questions.prompt: What does HTTPS primarily protect while a browser communicates with a website?
options: Data in transit between the browser and the server
All data stored on the user's device
The truth of every statement on the website
A server from every denial-of-service attack
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses TLS to protect the connection in transit and authenticate the server.

questions.prompt: Why validate untrusted input on the server?
options: Clients can send values that bypass interface checks
It removes the need for authorization
It guarantees the client device is secure
questions.explanation: Server-side validation is necessary because client-side checks can be bypassed.

questions.prompt: What is a standard way to reduce SQL injection risk in database queries?
options: Use parameterized queries for untrusted values
Concatenate raw input into SQL strings
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate data from SQL commands.

questions.prompt: What security benefit does multi-factor authentication provide?
options: It requires additional independent evidence during sign-in
It removes the need to protect accounts
It guarantees that a device has no malware
questions.explanation: A second factor can reduce account takeover risk when a password is compromised.

questions.prompt: What is a safer response to a suspicious attachment?
options: Do not open it and report it through the approved channel
Enter account credentials to inspect it
questions.explanation: Avoid interacting with suspicious files and report them so the appropriate team can assess them.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do after noticing a possible security incident?
options: Report it promptly using the organization's incident process
Delete logs before anyone sees them
Ignore it until a service fails
questions.explanation: Prompt reporting through established channels helps responders investigate and limit impact.
